bibliographic.title: Insights into the Interactions between Surfactin, Betaines and PAM: Surface Tension, Small-Angle Neutron Scattering and Small-Angle X-ray Scattering Study

bibliographic.abstract: The interactions between neutral polymer polyacrylamide (PAM) and the biosurfactant Surfactin and four betaines, N ­dodecyl­ N,N ­dimethyl­3 ­ammonio­ 1­propanesulfonate (SDDAB), N ­tetradecyl­ N,N ­dimethyl­3­ammonio­1­ propanesulfonate (STDAB), N ­hexadecyl­ N,N ­ dimethyl­3­ammonio­1­ propanesulfonate (SHDAB), and N ­dodecyl­ N,N ­dimethyl­2­ammonio­acetate (C12BE), in phosphate buffer solution (PBS) have been studied by surface tension measurements, small-angle neutron scattering (SANS), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) and rheological experiments. It has been confirmed that the length of alkyl chain is a key parameter of interaction between betaines and PAM. Differences in scattering contrast between X-ray and neutrons for surfactants and PAM molecules provide the opportunity to follow separately the changes of structure of PAM and surfactant aggregates. At concentrations of betaines higher than CMC (critical micelle concentration) and C2 (CMC of surfactant with the presence of polymer), spherical micelles are formed in betaines and betaines/PAM solutions. Transition from spherical to rod-like aggregates (micelles) has been observed in solutions of Surfactin and Surfactin/SDDAB (αSurfactin = 0.67 (molar fraction)) with addition of 0.8 wt% of PAM. The conformation change of PAM molecules only can be observed for Surfactin/SDDAB/PAM system in PBS. Viscosity values follow the structural changes suggested from scattering measurements i.e., gradually increases for mixtures PAM  Surfactin/PAM  Surfactin/SDDAB/PAM in PBS.

samples.sample_description: Surfactin-C15 isoform was separated by extraction with anhydrous ether, isolated with normal pressure ODS C18 column and purified by the RP-HPLC.
Polyacrylamide with average molecular weight of around 5,000,000-6,000,000.
SDDAB mixed with 0.8wt% PAM in PBS.
STDAB mixed with 0.8wt% PAM in PBS.
SHDAB mixed with 0.8wt% PAM in PBS.
C12BE mixed with 0.8wt% PAM in PBS.
Surfactin mixed with 0.8wt% PAM in PBS.
Surfactin/SDDAB mixed system with αsurfactin=0.67 and 0.8wt% PAM in PBS.

datasets.dataset_description: Surface tensions for aqueous solutions of pure Surfactin, SDDAB, STDAB, SHDAB, C12BE, Surfactin/SDDAB (αsurfactin=0.67), and each mixed with 0.8wt%PAM were measured over a wide concentration range to determine the CAC, CMC and C2.
SANS measurements were performed on samples prepared with 10 mM deuterium phosphate buffer solution (pD 7.4), with scattering vectors q ranging from 0.09 to 3.1 nm-1 at T=25.0±0.5 °C.
SAXS experiments were performed at 25 °C using a Pilatus 2M detector and synchrotron radiation with a wavelength λ = 1 Å, with measurements in the q interval ranging from 0.1 to 4 nm-1.
The stationary viscosity of the surfactant/polymer solutions was measured using a rotational rheometer at different shear rates in the interval from 0.1 s-1 to 1000 s-1 at a temperature of 30 °C.
